cohort: The cohort consisted of 810 women (48.7% preterm) with a mean age of 28.33 years, who experienced either preterm or term labor over a seven-year period at an educational hospital.
finding: The study identified intercourse during the previous week, multiparity, short interpregnancy interval, preeclampsia, fetal anomaly, rupture of membranes, hypertension, and amniotic fluid leak as risk factors for preterm labor, while iron consumption, cephalic presentation, systematic disease, history of caesarean section, prenatal care, and mother's weight were found to be protective factors.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over a seven-year period.
